key_insight: An E(3)-equivariant neural network learns molecular self-energy matrices on the imaginary-frequency axis, enabling accurate real-frequency spectra without a new explicit G₀W₀ calculation.
engineering_relevance: Given a density-functional reference, the trained model could reduce the cost of predicting molecular quasiparticle energies and spectral functions.
method: Predict complex, frequency-dependent correlation self-energy matrices from atomic species and coordinates using equivariant message passing.
Encode frequency as a network input or use frequency-specific output heads; take static exchange from the density-functional reference.
Continue predictions to real frequencies using a representation that enforces causality and non-negative spectral density.
evidence_signal: The frequency-conditioned model achieves sub-1-meV imaginary-axis matrix-element accuracy and frontier quasiparticle energies within a few tens of meV for water clusters, including an unseen tetramer, and diverse QM9 molecules.
watch_item: Results concern molecular benchmarks; transfer to polymers, composites, or extended solids remains unestablished, and inference still requires a density-functional reference.
paper_title: Learning the self-energy through equivariant neural networks
